title: Undifferentiated shock at the bedside (template)
summary: Template showing the practical-theory format: case → decision points → bedside how-to → pitfalls.
learning_objectives: Pick a first vasopressor and MAP target

case.vignette: A 58-year-old presents with fever, BP 78/40 mmHg, HR 124, warm peripheries, lactate 4.6 mmol/L.

sections.prompt: What is the most likely shock type?

options.feedback: Warm peripheries + fever + high lactate → septic (distributive).
Cold, clammy, raised JVP and pulmonary oedema would point here.
Look for tamponade, tension pneumothorax, massive PE.
